evals.prompt: Generate a deployment proposal and complete app-of-apps manifests for public image nginxdemos/hello:plain-text as demo scratch-hello at https://jakob-lingel.dev/demo/scratch-hello. Use fixture.md as the authoritative environment. Write only into the supplied output directory. No live cluster, networking, registry, git, bd or Terraform commands; don't edit real repositories. Include a deployment report explaining path behavior, TLS ownership, checks actually performed and remaining verification.
evals.expected_output: Coherent manifests for a public demo sharing the apex route/certificate without unnecessary DNS, secrets, duplicate TLS issuance or build setup; path forwarding is justified and live status is not invented.
expectations: Manifests route the exact demo prefix to a matching Service and workload port and justify forwarding the path unchanged.
The shared apex TLS owner is preserved without a cross-namespace TLS Secret reference, duplicate Certificate request or unnecessary DNS change.
The public root-required image receives no unnecessary pull credential, database or forced non-root UID, and direct Pod probes match its documented runtime.
Actual offline checks are distinguished from unperformed schema/admission/live verification and the mutable image tag is acknowledged.

evals.prompt: Generate complete app-of-apps manifests and narrowly scoped proposed infra edits for tool report-viewer using private ghcr.io/davidcode2/report-viewer:1.4.2 at reports.jakob-lingel.dev. Use fixture.md as authoritative. Write only into the supplied output directory. No live cluster, networking, registry, git, bd or Terraform commands; don't edit real repositories. Include required prerequisites and exact verification steps. The existing GitHub App repo credential in argocd already lets Argo read our Git repo.
evals.expected_output: Namespaced GHCR pull ExternalSecret and workload reference independent of Argo Git auth; proper SSM docker JSON mapping, scoped DNS, new-host TLS and no local Terraform execution.
expectations: A namespaced ExternalSecret materializes kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson from /shared/ghcr/dockerconfigjson and the Pod references that Secret.
The output distinguishes Argo Git credentials from GHCR image-pull access and adds no unnecessary IAM or SSM resources.
The proposed infra change adds only the reports CNAME and the Ingress requests TLS for reports.jakob-lingel.dev without an invented www host.
Runtime configuration matches UID 10001, port 8080, PUBLIC_URL and documented probes, with writable /tmp and no dependency on an unavailable reloader.
Verification covers registry Secret readiness, current Argo revision, ready service endpoints, DNS and TLS while honestly reporting no live deployment or Terraform execution.

evals.prompt: Generate a complete proposal and manifests for real tool field-notes using public ghcr.io/davidcode2/field-notes:2.3.0 at notes.jakob-lingel.dev, PostgreSQL 16 and 5Gi persistent uploads plus 10Gi database storage. Use fixture.md as authoritative. Keep uploaded files and the database when uninstalling. Include the required first-install migration and concrete backup/restore design. Write only into the supplied output directory. No live cluster, networking, registry, git, bd or Terraform commands; don't edit real repositories. Explain limitations and any unresolved inputs rather than inventing them.
evals.expected_output: First-install-safe secret/database/migration/app ordering, no single-writer overlap, correct PVC and credential mappings, local-path failure limitations, namespace-safe retention, and an honest backup destination blocker.
expectations: PostgreSQL and app credentials map to the existing SSM sources with correct documented env names, internal DB service and separate upload/database mounts.
First-install migration can run after database/Secret prerequisites and before app readiness without a PreSync dependency trap or WaitForFirstConsumer PVC-wave deadlock.
App and database rollout configuration avoids overlapping single-writer instances, and the report does not describe one-replica RWO as an application write lock.
Retention explicitly protects against both Argo PVC deletion and Namespace/Application cascade, and uninstall removes compute while keeping the requested data.
The proposal explains node-local storage failure limits, gives a workable off-node backup and restore design, and identifies unspecified backup inputs rather than claiming operational backups.
Checks distinguish offline results from live readiness, image digest, DNS/TLS, HCL CI and actual persistence/restore verification.
